questions.stem: Before uterine implantation, a conceptus is examined in section. Which developmental stage matches its cavity and cell arrangement?
options: Blastocyst
Morula
Single-cell zygote
Bilaminar embryonic disc

choice_rationales: A large cavity is enclosed by a thin cellular rim, with a compact inner cell mass at one pole. This choice describes a blastocyst, which is what the image shows.
A solid ball of cells would not have this dominant internal cavity. This choice describes a morula.
The image has many cells and a cavity, not one undivided cell. This choice describes a zygote.
Two flat embryonic cell layers are not the dominant structure shown. This choice describes a bilaminar embryonic disc.

Complex cyst with a mural nodule
Irregular mass with spiculated margins
Anechoic cyst with posterior enhancement

choice_rationales: The interior is anechoic and the tissue behind it is bright, not shadowed. This choice describes a solid hypoechoic mass with shadowing (malignancy).
No solid mural projection interrupts the black cavity. This choice describes a complex cyst with a mural nodule (papilloma or carcinoma).
The contour is smooth and oval rather than irregular or spiculated. This choice describes a spiculated malignant mass.

questions.condition_overview: Fibrocystic changes are the most common benign breast condition in premenopausal women and cause cyclical pain and lumpiness. Findings include cysts, stromal fibrosis, and adenosis. Nonproliferative changes carry no added cancer risk, whereas proliferative changes (usual ductal hyperplasia, sclerosing adenosis) carry a mild increase, and proliferative disease with atypia a moderate increase.

Widely spaced normal double-layered ducts
Intraluminal epithelial proliferation
Isolated single cells infiltrating stroma
questions.explanation: Crowded epithelial cells bridge and partially fill one expanded ductal lumen. The cells remain clustered inside the duct rather than forming isolated stromal files.
choice_rationales: The central structure is an epithelial duct, not injured fat. This choice describes fat necrosis.
The many intraluminal cell layers exceed a normal thin duct lining. This choice describes normal ducts.
Crowded epithelial cells bridge and partially fill one expanded ductal lumen. This choice describes usual ductal hyperplasia, which is what the image shows.
The cells remain clustered inside the duct rather than forming isolated stromal files. This choice describes invasive carcinoma.

questions.condition_overview: Usual ductal hyperplasia is a benign proliferation of ductal epithelial cells that fills and expands the duct in an irregular, streaming pattern with slit-like peripheral spaces. Cells are heterogeneous, a mix of luminal and myoepithelial cells, and stain patchy for CK5/6. It carries a slight increase in later breast cancer risk (about 1.5 to 2 times).

Inflammation around disrupted fat spaces
Cribriform epithelial growth inside a duct
Single-file stromal infiltration

questions.condition_overview: Fat necrosis is a benign inflammatory process of breast adipose tissue that follows trauma, surgery, or radiation. Fat cell death produces a firm, sometimes painless mass that can mimic carcinoma on examination and imaging, with calcifications. Histology shows foamy macrophages, multinucleated giant cells, and fibrosis. It carries no increased risk of cancer.

questions.condition_overview: Brenner tumor is a usually benign ovarian surface epithelial-stromal tumor composed of nests of urothelial-like (transitional) epithelium in a dense fibrous stroma. The epithelial cells have oval nuclei with longitudinal grooves, called coffee-bean nuclei, and nests may contain small cysts. Most are incidental, small, solid, and cured by oophorectomy.

questions.condition_overview: Condylomata acuminata (genital warts) are benign papillary squamous proliferations caused mainly by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11, spread by sexual contact. They appear as soft, exophytic, cauliflower-like lesions on the vulva, penis, perineum, or perianal skin. Microscopically there is acanthosis, papillomatosis, hyperkeratosis or parakeratosis, and koilocytes, which are squamous cells with a wrinkled, enlarged nucleus surrounded by a perinuclear clear halo. They are treated with topical agents, cryotherapy, or excision, and recur often. The HPV vaccine prevents them.

Within the skull bones only
Within an extra-axial crescent
Confined to the cortical sulci

choice_rationales: The bright deposits follow the margins of the enlarged lateral ventricles. This choice describes congenital CMV infection (periventricular calcifications), which is what the image shows.
The arrows end deep to the skull on ventricular margins. This choice describes a skull abnormality.
The deposits are central and periventricular, not a peripheral crescent. This choice describes subdural hematoma.
The large arrows point to ventricular walls rather than cortical sulci. This choice describes cortical calcifications (such as toxoplasmosis).

questions.condition_overview: Congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV) is the most common congenital infection, acquired by transplacental transmission, usually after primary maternal infection. Many newborns are asymptomatic, but severe cases show microcephaly, periventricular calcifications, chorioretinitis, hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, petechiae, and sensorineural hearing loss. Tissue shows enlarged cells with large basophilic intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a halo (owl's eye). Diagnosis is by PCR of urine or saliva in the first weeks of life, and treatment is ganciclovir or valganciclovir.

questions.stem: A child is evaluated for late findings of an infection acquired before birth. Which change in the upper permanent incisors supports that history?
options: Multiple extra incisors
Complete absence of incisors
Diffuse gingival overgrowth
Notched incisal edges
questions.explanation: The paired notched incisors illustrate the Hutchinson teeth appearance associated with congenital syphilis. Examine the biting edges of the teeth that are present instead of counting teeth or assessing the gingiva.
choice_rationales: The striking finding is the shape of the existing incisors, not extra teeth. This choice describes supernumerary teeth.
The incisors are present and visible. This choice describes anodontia.
The abnormality is in the tooth edges rather than enlarged gingiva. This choice describes gingival hyperplasia.
Both upper central incisors have a central indentation along their biting edges. This choice describes Hutchinson teeth (congenital syphilis), which is what the image shows.

questions.condition_overview: Congenital syphilis results from transplacental passage of Treponema pallidum, mostly after the first trimester. Early disease causes rash with desquamation, snuffles, hepatosplenomegaly, and osteochondritis. Late features include Hutchinson triad (notched, peg-shaped central incisors called Hutchinson teeth, interstitial keratitis, and eighth nerve deafness), saddle nose, mulberry molars, and saber shins. It is prevented by maternal screening and penicillin treatment during pregnancy.

questions.condition_overview: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is a malignant proliferation of ductal epithelial cells confined by the basement membrane. Patterns include comedo (high grade with central necrosis and calcifications), solid, cribriform, and papillary. It is usually detected as mammographic microcalcifications. Left untreated, a proportion progresses to invasive ductal carcinoma. Treatment is lumpectomy with radiation, or mastectomy, and endocrine therapy if ER positive.

questions.condition_overview: Mature cystic teratoma is the most common ovarian germ cell tumor and is benign. It is a unilocular cyst lined by skin with sebaceous glands and hair follicles, containing hair and greasy sebum and often teeth, bone, cartilage, thyroid, and brain tissue derived from all three germ layers. It is a frequent cause of adnexal masses in young women, is bilateral in about 10 to 15 percent, and can cause torsion or, rarely, autoimmune anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis. A rare complication is malignant transformation to squamous cell carcinoma. Imaging shows fat that loses signal on fat suppression.

questions.stem: In a solid ovarian mass, compare the large cells in the nests with the much smaller dark cells between them. Which pairing fits?
options: Spindle cells with mature adipocytes
Mucin-laden signet-ring cells with fibroblasts
Thyroid follicular cells surrounding colloid
Large pale cells with small dark lymphocytes
questions.explanation: Large pale tumor cells with conspicuous nuclei are interspersed with much smaller dark lymphocytes. The tumor cells are rounded and pale, not spindle shaped, and mature fat is absent.
choice_rationales: The tumor cells are rounded and pale, not spindle shaped, and mature fat is absent. This choice describes a spindle cell tumor with fat.
Large mucin vacuoles displacing nuclei to the edge are not shown. This choice describes signet-ring cell carcinoma.
The field lacks colloid-filled follicles. This choice describes a thyroid tumor.

questions.condition_overview: Dysgerminoma is the ovarian counterpart of testicular seminoma and the most common malignant ovarian germ cell tumor, typically in young women. It forms a solid, pale, fleshy, lobulated mass. Microscopically large round cells with clear cytoplasm, distinct cell borders, and central nuclei with prominent nucleoli are arranged in nests separated by fibrous septa infiltrated by lymphocytes. Cells are OCT3/4, CD117, and PLAP positive. Tumors are highly radiosensitive and chemosensitive with an excellent prognosis. It can occur in gonadal dysgenesis, such as Swyer syndrome.

questions.stem: How does estrogen excretion change after the point marked menopause on this graph?
options: Falls immediately to zero
Declines toward a low plateau
Continues with large cyclic peaks
Rises steadily to its lifetime maximum
questions.explanation: The height of the curve at the menopausal transition and the slope after it tell different stories. The trace falls and then levels off above the baseline, consistent with continued nonfollicular estrogen production discussed in R4.
choice_rationales: Postmenopausal estrogen excretion stays above zero, even after the initial decline. This choice describes an abrupt loss of all estrogen production.
Postmenopausal estrogen excretion declines and then settles at a low plateau above zero. This choice describes the normal postmenopausal fall to a low plateau, which is what the figure shows.

The large cyclic estrogen peaks occur during the reproductive years. After menopause the curve settles at a low level without those repeated peaks. This choice describes persistence of cyclic ovarian estrogen peaks.
Estrogen excretion falls after menopause. The plotted lifetime peaks are earlier, during the reproductive years. This choice describes a rise in estrogen to its lifetime maximum.

questions.stem: Using both panels, which pair of plotted ranges has the earliest left boundary for its sex?
options: Underarm hair in girls and overall body-shape changes in boys
Breast budding in girls and growth of scrotum/testes in boys
Menarche in girls and growth spurt in boys
Adult breast size in girls and facial hair in boys
questions.explanation: The breast-budding range begins at the left edge of the girls panel, while scrotal/testicular growth begins among the earliest ranges in the boys panel. Adult breast size and facial hair begin well after breast budding and scrotal or testicular growth, which start among the earliest ranges.
choice_rationales: Underarm hair and body-shape change begin after breast budding and scrotal or testicular growth, which start among the earliest ranges. This choice describes the sequence of pubic hair development in girls and general body-shape change in boys.

The breast-budding range begins at the left edge of the girls panel, while scrotal/testicular growth begins among the earliest ranges in the boys panel. This choice describes the onset of thelarche in girls and testicular enlargement in boys, which is what the image shows.

questions.condition_overview: Placenta accreta spectrum describes abnormally deep placental implantation resulting from a defective decidua basalis, often after a previous cesarean section or other uterine surgery. In accreta villi attach to the myometrium, in increta they invade into it, and in percreta they penetrate through the full thickness to the serosa and may invade adjacent organs. After delivery the placenta does not separate and causes life-threatening hemorrhage, and hysterectomy is often required.

questions.condition_overview: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a nodular proliferation of glands and stroma in the periurethral transition zone, driven by dihydrotestosterone and increasing with age. questions.condition_overview: Prostatic adenocarcinoma is the most common nonskin cancer in men and typically arises in the peripheral zone, so it presents late with urinary symptoms and is often found by PSA or digital rectal examination. questions.condition_overview: Dysgerminoma is the ovarian counterpart of testicular seminoma and the most common malignant ovarian germ cell tumor, typically in young women. It forms a solid, pale, fleshy, lobulated mass. questions.condition_overview: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma is the most common cervical cancer and arises from persistently infected high-risk HPV lesions at the transformation zone through HSIL. Nests of malignant squamous cells with keratin pearls and intercellular bridges invade the cervical stroma. It presents with postcoital or abnormal bleeding, or may be found by screening. Treatment is surgery for early disease and chemoradiation with brachytherapy for advanced disease.

questions.condition_overview: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) is HPV-driven dysplasia of the cervical squamous epithelium graded by the depth of epithelium replaced by atypical cells (CIN 1 lower third, CIN 2 two thirds, CIN 3 full thickness). questions.condition_overview: Extramammary Paget disease is an uncommon intraepidermal adenocarcinoma, most often on the vulva of older women, that presents as a red, scaly or eczematous, itchy plaque. Microscopically large pale cells with abundant cytoplasm and atypical nuclei are scattered singly and in nests among the keratinocytes of the epidermis, sometimes extending into skin appendages. The cells contain intracytoplasmic mucin (mucicarmine and PAS positive) and are CK7 positive, unlike squamous cells. It is usually confined to the epidermis, but some cases are associated with an underlying adnexal or visceral carcinoma, and the invasive form carries a worse prognosis. Treatment is wide excision.

questions.condition_overview: Prostatic adenocarcinoma is the most common nonskin cancer in men and typically arises in the peripheral zone, so it presents late with urinary symptoms and is often found by PSA or digital rectal examination. questions.condition_overview: Endometriosis is the presence of functional endometrial glands and stroma outside the uterus, most often on the ovaries, pelvic peritoneum, and rectovaginal septum, and rarely in the bladder, vagina, or even the lung. Ectopic tissue responds to cyclic hormones, bleeds, and causes chronic inflammation and fibrosis. Patients have dysmenorrhea, pelvic pain, dyspareunia, and infertility. Catamenial symptoms, such as thoracic or bladder symptoms with menses, suggest distant implants.

questions.condition_overview: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a nodular proliferation of glands and stroma in the periurethral transition zone, driven by dihydrotestosterone and increasing with age. Enlarged nodules compress the prostatic urethra, causing hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia, and incomplete emptying, with risks of retention, infection, and bladder hypertrophy. Microscopically there are large glands with papillary infoldings with two cell layers, and basal cells are preserved. It does not become cancer. Treatment is with alpha-blockers, 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors, or resection.

questions.condition_overview: Menopause is the permanent end of menstruation after 12 months of amenorrhea, at an average age of about 51, caused by depletion of ovarian follicles. Estradiol and inhibin B fall, so FSH (and later LH) rise, and the main estrogen becomes extragonadal estrone from adipose aromatization of androstenedione. Perimenopause is the preceding transition with irregular cycles, and treatment is symptomatic, including hormone therapy in selected patients.

questions.condition_overview: Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) are benign smooth muscle tumors and the most common tumor in women, growth being estrogen and progesterone dependent. They are classified as submucosal (beneath the endometrium, causing the most bleeding), intramural (within the wall), or subserosal (beneath the serosa, causing pressure effects). They are well-circumscribed, firm, whorled, white-tan masses with interlacing bundles of uniform spindle cells without atypia. Symptoms include heavy menstrual bleeding, pelvic pressure, and infertility, and they shrink after menopause. Malignant transformation (leiomyosarcoma) is rare.

questions.condition_overview: Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) are benign smooth muscle tumors and the most common tumor in women, growth being estrogen and progesterone dependent. They are classified as submucosal (beneath the endometrium, causing the most bleeding), intramural (within the wall), or subserosal (beneath the serosa, causing pressure effects). They are well-circumscribed, firm, whorled, white-tan masses with interlacing bundles of uniform spindle cells without atypia. Symptoms include heavy menstrual bleeding, pelvic pressure, and infertility, and they shrink after menopause. Malignant transformation (leiomyosarcoma) is rare.
questions.case_context: A 49-year-old woman has bleeding and a saline infusion sonogram showing a mass in the cavity. Color Doppler shows blood flow distributed throughout the lesion. In a second patient with a similar mass, color Doppler shows a single feeding vessel.

questions.condition_overview: Atypical endometrial hyperplasia (endometrioid intraepithelial neoplasia) is the precursor of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma. It results from unopposed estrogen from obesity, anovulation, or estrogen therapy. Crowded glands with little intervening stroma are lined by cells with rounded, enlarged nuclei, loss of polarity, and nuclear stratification, which differ from the surrounding glands. A substantial fraction coexist with carcinoma, so treatment is progestin therapy or hysterectomy, based on the patient's wishes.

questions.condition_overview: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma is the most common cervical cancer and arises from persistently infected high-risk HPV lesions at the transformation zone through HSIL. Nests of malignant squamous cells with keratin pearls and intercellular bridges invade the cervical stroma. It presents with postcoital or abnormal bleeding, or may be found by screening. Staging uses tumor size, parametrial, pelvic wall, and nodal spread. Advanced disease can obstruct the ureters and cause hydronephrosis and renal failure, which is a major cause of death. Treatment is surgery for early disease and chemoradiation with brachytherapy for advanced disease.

questions.condition_overview: A hydrocele is a collection of serous fluid between the layers of the tunica vaginalis surrounding the testis. In infants it results from a patent processus vaginalis that allows peritoneal fluid to enter the scrotum (communicating hydrocele). In adults it can follow trauma, infection, or tumor. questions.condition_overview: Adenomyosis is the presence of benign endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium, deeper than the usual endometrial-myometrial junction. The uterus enlarges symmetrically and has a thickened, trabeculated wall with small cystic or hemorrhagic foci. Patients have heavy, painful menses and a boggy, tender uterus. Microscopically there are islands of endometrial-type glands with stromal cuffs among smooth muscle bundles, with hypertrophy of the surrounding muscle. On MRI it thickens the junctional zone. Definitive treatment is hysterectomy.

questions.condition_overview: Menopause is the permanent end of menstruation after 12 months of amenorrhea, at an average age of about 51, caused by depletion of ovarian follicles. Estradiol and inhibin B fall, so FSH (and later LH) rise, and the main estrogen becomes extragonadal estrone from adipose aromatization of androstenedione. Estrogen deficiency causes hot flashes, vaginal atrophy, sleep disturbance, bone loss and osteoporosis, and adverse lipid changes. Perimenopause is the preceding transition with irregular cycles, and treatment is symptomatic, including hormone therapy in selected patients.

questions.condition_overview: Osteoporosis is reduced bone mass and microarchitectural deterioration that predisposes to fragility fractures of the vertebrae, hip, and wrist. After menopause, estrogen loss increases RANKL-mediated osteoclast activity, causing rapid trabecular bone loss. Serum calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase are normal. Diagnosis uses DEXA with T-score of -2.5 or below, and treatment includes calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, bisphosphonates, denosumab, and anabolic agents.

questions.condition_overview: Neonatal jaundice is elevated bilirubin in newborns, which is physiologic in most babies during the first week because of immature hepatic UDP-glucuronosyltransferase and a high red cell turnover. Jaundice in the first 24 hours or conjugated hyperbilirubinemia is pathologic. Unconjugated bilirubin can cross the blood-brain barrier and cause kernicterus (basal ganglia injury). Treatment is phototherapy, converting bilirubin to a water-soluble isomer, and exchange transfusion in severe cases.
